To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enhanced secretion of a mutant beta-lactoglobin (beta-LG) in Saccharomyes cerevisiae resulting form a single amino acid replacement was caused by the accelerated transport of the mutant protein from the endoplasmatic reticulum (Er) to the Golgi apparatus.
a single amino acid mutation of Trp(19)-Tyr(19) in beta-lactoglobuin resulted in a 6-fold increase in the secretion efficiency in Saccharomyes cerevisiae.
the enhanced level and speed of secretion of the W19 beta-LG mutant are the result of the improved folding ability in the ER of Saccharomyces cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method of improving the efficiency of heterologous protein production by yeast.
the development of a novel approach to the improvement of protein secretion efficiency.

the elucidation of the relationship between the secretion efficiency of a protein and its molecular properties, which is of significance for the improvement of the secretion of foreign proteins in yeast cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accelerated secretion of W19 is due to the increased stability of the protein and its ability to maintain its native structure in the ER of yeast cells.

the enhanced secretion of mutant beta-LG was caused by the acceleration of the secretion process due to its improved folding ability, and that the folding ability of the protein was a crucial determinant of its secretion efficiency.
the accelerated secretion of W19 is the result of a combination of its increased folding efficiency and its ability to maintain a specific folded structure in the yeast ER.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the secretion efficiency is enhanced by improving the folding ability of secretory protein.
the secretion efficiency of a protein is determined in the ER, and is dependent upon the folding ability of the protein and the amount of BiP.

the secretion efficiency of beta-LG is improved when the protein is unfolded in the ER and that the protein can be unfolded when the stability of the folded structure in the ER is low and when the protein maintains a specific folded structure in the yeast cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the folding of the target protein inside the ER is an important factor determining the secretion efficiency.
the secretion efficiency of a protein is determined by its folding ability in the ER.
the secretion efficiency of a secretory protein can be improved by increasing the speed of secretion.
